objectClass.primaryType: single-storey branded retail shop unit (telecom operator branch)
motionPotential: none - fixed building shell; the entrance leaves are modelled as part of the static shopfront and are not articulated
objectClass.notes: Exterior shell only. The plate shows a shop interior through the glazing; none of it is modelled, so the glazing is authored as a tinted mostly-opaque SURFACE rather than a transparent window. Every observed finish is flat and unpatterned; the only patterned regions are two printed graphics (the AIS sign face and the spandrel posters), both routed through a canvas applied AFTER material construction.

reasoning: Silhouette is a single parapet-topped cuboid - trivially simple, scored 2. The difficulty in this subject is NOT its shape.

Repetition density is high (5): mullions, transoms, condensers and duct segments are all repeated boxes, which is what keeps the model inside a hero2x geometry ceiling when they share one instanced unit box.
Local detail density is 5: the identity of this prop is almost entirely surface treatment (brand green, sign graphic, spandrel bays, two-tone front elevation) rather than form.
Occlusion risk 4: one three-quarter view leaves the right side wall and the whole rear wall unseen. Mitigated, not eliminated, by the registry brief specifying those faces as plain render.
Action-readiness need 1: a fixed building shell with no moving parts, one root pivot and no sockets.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate depth, but with a hard budget-driven shape to the component tree. The thaikit hero2x class allows 8 unique geometries, 12 draw calls and 8 materials - HALF the sibling 7-Eleven building's hero4x ceiling. Unique geometries is the binding axis, because the generator bakes component dimensions into vertex data via geometry.scale(), so every distinct componentTree box is a distinct geometry. The tree is therefore designed in the blockout to 7 component geometries plus ONE shared unit box carrying every repeated part as InstancedMesh clusters: 8 of 8. Repetition systems are mandatory here, not optional - authoring the mullions, transoms, condensers and duct segments as components would blow the geometry ceiling on its own.

detailInventory.note: Twelve identity-defining details against a floor of six. Each maps to a component.localFeatures or material.localOverrides entry, never prose alone. Zone crops from build_detail_inventory.py grid-3x3 are in detail-zones/; the named crops in crops/ are the component-zone scan that actually drove this list.

details.description: White AIS swoosh (a curved crescent/wing) followed by the 'AIS' wordmark in a bold rounded sans, centred on the green sign face.
The green lightbox tray stands proud of the white fascia band with a visible drop shadow along its lower edge and a thin lighter edge return on its sides.
A horizontal reveal groove and a vertical panel joint in the white fascia band, right of the sign tray.
Two full-height opaque vivid yellow-green panels bracketing the glazed bays at each end of the shopfront. Opaque vinyl-faced spandrel, not glass.
A pale, near-white poster rectangle applied to each green spandrel bay, upper-middle of the panel.
A horizontal aluminium transom rail running across the glazed bays near the head, plus a lower rail near the sill.
A wider vertical meeting stile at the centre door pair carrying a vertical pull handle.
A lighter cream-grey cap course along the top of the parapet, slightly proud of the wall face on both sides.
Vertical darker streaks running down the render immediately below the parapet, heaviest at the corners.
A single flush service door set in a shallow recessed reveal on the left side wall, cream on cream, with a small lever handle.
A grey concrete kerb/sill course under the full width of the glazing, standing proud of the render face.
A circular fan grille disc with a vertical louvre strip beside it on each rooftop condenser's outward face.

componentTree.name: Building shell: side and rear walls with parapet
componentTree.topologyRationale: The -X, -Z and +X walls are one continuous painted render surface and one extrusion. Splitting them into three components would spend three draw calls, for the life of the prop, to express one skin. The +Z wall is separate ONLY because a plan extrusion cannot carry a vertical opening, and the shopfront opening is the identity feature of the front elevation.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: U-shaped footprint ring extruded 4.60 m upward: the -X, -Z and +X walls at 0.20 m thickness, open on +Z where the facade wall takes over. Hollow by construction. The parapet is the same extrusion continuing past the roof deck at 3.90 m -- it is NOT a separate proud element, because the plate shows one unbroken render surface from ground to coping.

copingProfile.note: Lighter cream-grey cap projecting proud of both parapet faces with a drip edge, measured off crops/side-wall.png at 0.85 confidence.

geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: Eight profile points, one extrusion step: 8 side quads plus caps, about 60 triangles.
geometryDescriptor.shapeSpaceNote: Profile is authored in (sx, sy) = (worldX, -worldZ). The component carries rotationEuler [-pi/2, 0, 0], mapping the shape plane onto the ground plane and the extrusion axis onto world +Y. Extrude components are NOT unit-scaled by the generator -- profile units are real metres, so these are the building's actual footprint coordinates.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The U's open ends stop at sy=-3.30, which is worldZ=+3.30 -- the facade wall's BACK face -- not at +3.50 where its front face is. Two surfaces in the same plane facing the SAME direction tear into interleaved triangles as the camera moves; this joint is instead a butt of OPPOSED faces, which is how solids are meant to meet. A first draft of this profile put the open ends at +3.50 and would have shipped the identical defect the sibling 7-Eleven had in eight places. The rear outer face at sy=+3.50 is worldZ=-3.50, so the footprint still comes out at exactly the declared 7.0 m.
geometryDescriptor.copingHandoffNote: The walls stop at y=4.52 and the parapet COPING owns the top 0.16 m, ending at the declared 4.60 m. That split exists to avoid a z-fight, not for its own sake: a coping band laid on top of a wall that also reaches 4.60 puts two +Y faces in the same plane, which is the coincident co-facing case this prop has been careful about throughout. With the wall at 4.52 its top face is BURIED inside the coping's 4.44-4.60 span and only the coping's own top is exposed. Total height is unchanged at the declared 4.60 m.

localFeatures.notes: Lighter cream-grey cap standing 0.05 m proud of both parapet faces. BUILT, by the parapet-coping cluster, after the material-pass comparison showed the plate's cap reading clearly lighter than the wall while the model's parapet was a single flat cream. It carries the white-panel material, costs one draw call -- the prop's last -- and costs ZERO unique geometries because it shares the clusters' unit box.
Vertical run-off streaking below the coping drip, heaviest at the corners.

Service door on the -X wall, read as a shadow reveal around the leaf. Built by the side-wall-fittings cluster as a proud architrave with a less-proud leaf; see that system's rationale for the stated relief deviation.

geometryDescriptor.scaleConvention: NO `scale` key on transform, deliberately. generate_threejs_factory.py's scale_vector() SHORT-CIRCUITS on the presence of transform.scale and returns it verbatim; only when the key is ABSENT does it fall through to sizing the unit box from dimensions.width/height/depth. An authored `scale: [1, 1, 1]` therefore reads as 'this box is one metre cubed', and every box in a first draft of this spec collapsed to a unit cube -- the glazing rendered as a 1 m box floating in a 6.8 m opening. The extrude components are the exact opposite and MUST keep scale: [1, 1, 1]: their profile2D points are already in real metres, so falling through to dimensions would rescale an 8 m building by a further 8x4.6x7.

componentTree.topologyRationale: A thin graphic FACE, not the whole tray. The tray's proud return is a separate InstancedMesh cluster on the shared unit box, which costs one draw call and zero unique geometries. Splitting it this way is what lets the printed AIS mark live on a 0.03 m plate whose side faces are hidden inside the return -- a canvas map on a BoxGeometry lands on all six faces, so a deep tray would have carried a squashed slice of the mark down each edge.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: single hard-edged box; no bevel, no subdivision
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: 1x1x1 segments: 12 triangles. Triangles are not the binding axis here.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Front face at z=+3.635, standing 0.035 m proud of the fascia band's +3.60. The surrounding tray return spans +3.52 to +3.645 and OVERLAPS this plate's edges, so no two co-facing surfaces share a plane.
geometryDescriptor.scaleConvention: NO `scale` key on transform, deliberately. generate_threejs_factory.py's scale_vector() SHORT-CIRCUITS on the presence of transform.scale and returns it verbatim; only when the key is ABSENT does it fall through to sizing the unit box from dimensions.width/height/depth. An authored `scale: [1, 1, 1]` therefore reads as 'this box is one metre cubed', and every box in a first draft of this spec collapsed to a unit cube -- the glazing rendered as a 1 m box floating in a 6.8 m opening. The extrude components are the exact opposite and MUST keep scale: [1, 1, 1]: their profile2D points are already in real metres, so falling through to dimensions would rescale an 8 m building by a further 8x4.6x7.

evidence: extract_pbr_evidence on material-crops/render-cream.png measures valueRange 0.080 and heightP90Gradient 0.0200 over a 186x200 px field: no high-frequency component survives at plate resolution, and the extractor itself warns 'low high-frequency detail weakens normal/roughness inference'.

textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely. That function writes FIVE canvases per material pixel by pixel in JavaScript, at a cost that is the SQUARE of textureResolution; seven materials at 1024 would cost roughly 13 s inside createObjectModel before the drawer could show anything, on a kit aimed at low-end integrated GPUs. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set present the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding the authored albedo -- which is what renders a cream building mid-grey. No textureResolution, referencePbr, textureProjection or surfaceFrequencyBands is carried here; the validator enforces both halves of the declaration.

materials.materialPipelineNote: material_region_analysis + apply_material_analysis were run and their PROVENANCE is kept -- materialFamily/Subtype/Finish, referenceMaterialId, materialReference, materialEvidence and textureAnalysis all come from that chain, and this material's region resolved to its canonical profile with status 'proceed'. What was NOT kept: the chain also wrote textureResolution, referencePbr and textureProjection onto every material, and overwrote the authored roughness and metalness with the profile's generic priors. A 0.06 m mullion is about 9 px on a 1024 plate, so no crop isolates it -- the comparator masked one render crop down to 22% coverage and kept the flanking GLASS rather than the metal, and it warns 'foreground mask is tiny; material extraction is likely unreliable' on the plate side. The plate's framing is also genuinely darker than any correct albedo would make it, because it is backlit by a dim shop interior that this exterior shell does not have. Driving deltaE to zero against that crop would mean baking the plate's lighting into base colour, which the material rules forbid outright. So the value is set to the darkest reading that is still an albedo, and the residual gap is reported.
materials.profileDeviation: The canonical profile resolved for this material (metal.aluminum) declares requiredMaps, and the compatibility check then fails it for having no UV/textureProjection contract. The requirement is waived here, recorded rather than deleted, for two reasons that are both properties of this pipeline rather than oversights. FIRST, img2threejs emits CODE and no textures: there is no baked map to bind, the material is declared textureless on measured evidence, and adding a textureProjection to satisfy the check would re-enable makeProceduralTextureSet and force color to white and roughness to 1 -- destroying the very albedo this material pass spent its rounds measuring. SECOND, the profile is evidence about what KIND of surface this is -- it is what let the region resolve at 0.79 and 0.86 confidence -- and its map list describes a photoreal metal workflow, not a low-end-GPU browser prop. This material is also bound to no componentTree entry by design: it is carried entirely by an InstancedMesh cluster, which the componentTree does not model, so no component could supply the uvContract the check looks for.

materials.finishStyle: hot-dip galvanised steel, semi-matte with weathering

evidence: heightP90Gradient 0.00692 -- the LOWEST of the seven crops -- on a surface whose valueRange of 0.519 comes entirely from staining and cast shadow between units.

The rooftop plant is visible only from above the parapet line. Spending five synthesised canvases on zinc spangle nobody in a first-person view will ever see is the clearest textureless case in this prop.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely. That function writes FIVE canvases per material pixel by pixel in JavaScript, at a cost that is the SQUARE of textureResolution; seven materials at 1024 would cost roughly 13 s inside createObjectModel before the drawer could show anything, on a kit aimed at low-end integrated GPUs. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set present the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding the authored albedo -- which is what renders a cream building mid-grey. No textureResolution, referencePbr, textureProjection or surfaceFrequencyBands is carried here; the validator enforces both halves of the declaration.

materials.metalnessNote: LOWERED from the physically-correct bare-metal value after the structural-pass render. A metalness near 1 has almost no diffuse term and gets its entire appearance from what it REFLECTS; thaikit's render harness lights analytically -- a hemisphere and three directional lights, no environment map and no PMREM -- so there is nothing to reflect and the surface renders near-black. The structural-pass render showed the condensers and duct as black boxes. This is not a harness quirk to work around either: this is a browser FPS prop for low-end integrated GPUs, where a level's lighting is very often analytic for the same performance reason, so a material that only reads under IBL is the wrong choice for the kit. The sibling 7-Eleven capped its aluminium at 0.35 and its galvanised at 0.30 for this exact reason. Roughness is nudged up with it so the specular lobe still carries the finish.

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout: closed clay mass, measured not asserted. Rendered bounds are exactly -4..4 x 0..4.6 x -3.5..3.5 m, the declared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 module. At the solved review pose (azimuth 320, elevation 18 -- the first pose that does NOT clip the frame) with framing normalised by height and centre, silhouette IoU is 0.838, aspectRatioDelta 0.021, scaleDelta 0.021, bilateralSymmetryError 0.038: the last three inside threshold, IoU 1.2 points short of 0.85. That shortfall is accounted for rather than waved through -- the fascia band, sign tray and kerb all stand PROUD of the facade and contribute to the plate's outline, and all three are meso and do not exist yet. TWO REAL DEFECTS were found and fixed here. (1) The U-ring profile put the shell's open ends at z=+3.50, exactly coplanar and co-facing with the facade wall's front face -- the identical defect the sibling 7-Eleven shipped in eight places. Moved to +3.30, the facade's BACK face, making it an opposed butt joint. (2) Every box component collapsed to a unit cube: scale_vector() short-circuits on the presence of transform.scale and only falls through to dimensions when the key is ABSENT, so an authored scale [1,1,1] read as 'one metre cubed' and the glazing rendered as a 1 m box inside a 6.8 m opening. The key is now removed from all five boxes and deliberately KEPT on the two extrudes, whose profile2D points are already in real metres. Also reclassified glazing and roof deck meso -> macro: turntable_gate measured the front silhouette as a 45% interior hole, and a mass open at the front and the roof is not a blockout of a building.

reviewHistory.summary:
Structural pass: every component and all four instanced clusters are built, and the four budget axes now measure on real geometry rather than on projection -- 1392 triangles / 16000, 11 draw calls / 12, 7 materials / 8, 8 unique geometries / 8. The geometry axis landing exactly on 8 confirms the blockout's central bet: seven component geometries plus ONE unit BoxGeometry shared across 31 instanced boxes in four clusters. Authored as components those 31 boxes would have been 31 more geometries and 31 more draw calls.

TURNTABLE GATE NOW PASSES (holed=false, covered=true). It failed at blockout with a 45% interior hole at azimuth 0; promoting the glazing and roof deck to macro closed it.

ONE REAL DEFECT found and fixed at this pass. The structural render showed the rooftop condensers and duct as BLACK boxes. Cause: aluminium was authored at metalness 0.85 and galvanised at 0.72 -- physically right for bare metal, and wrong here. A near-1 metalness has almost no diffuse term and takes its entire appearance from what it reflects, and thaikit's harness lights analytically (one hemisphere, three directional, no environment map, no PMREM), so there is nothing to reflect. Lowered to 0.35 and 0.30 with roughness raised to compensate, matching the sibling 7-Eleven's values. This is not a harness workaround: a browser FPS prop for low-end integrated GPUs is very often lit analytically for the same performance reason, so a material that only reads under IBL is the wrong choice for this kit.

Also widened the sign 5.40 -> 5.80 m: measured against the plate the sign spans about 82% of the shopfront opening and at 5.40 it spanned 78%. The tray return was widened with it.

SILHOUETTE, and an instrument finding. diagnose_render reports IoU 0.842 against a threshold of 0.85, with aspectRatioDelta 0.031, scaleDelta 0.031, bilateralSymmetryError 0.036 and maxDeltaE 13.5 all INSIDE their thresholds. The IoU shortfall is an artifact of the measurement, and the artifact was identified rather than assumed: a silhouette mask thresholded against the backdrop colour punches false holes wherever the SUBJECT is near that colour, and this plate's shop interior seen through the glazing is very close to its mid-grey backdrop. A difference overlay showed those false holes directly. Re-measured with interior holes flood-filled from the border on BOTH images -- which repairs the thresholding artifact without touching either outline -- the true silhouette IoU is 0.9079, comfortably above 0.85. Two independent signals agree that the shape is right: the rendered bounds are exactly the declared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m module, and the projected aspect at the solved pose is 1.379 against the plate's 1.339.

reviewHistory.summary:
Lighting pass. The prop carries lighting in three places and each is recorded rather than left implicit.

lightingFromPhoto holds the plate's own rig, read off the render: a soft key from upper front-left (the -X wall shows a gentle value falloff toward the front corner and the coping casts a short shadow onto the deck), a hemisphere fill bouncing off the mid-grey backdrop, and a weak rim separating the coping from that backdrop. Exposure 1.0 with ACESFilmic tone mapping, chosen for a specific reason: the sign's saturated green sits directly beside a high-value white fascia, and a linear response clips both toward white. thaikit's own harness independently uses ACESFilmic, so the model is reviewed under the response it was authored for.

Contact shadow is treated as a real requirement, not a checkbox. The prop is floor-placed so the shell casts to the ground plane, and INSIDE the model two internal contacts do the work that makes the front elevation read: the coping casts onto the roof deck, and the fascia band casts onto the glazing head. Those two shadows are what make the facade's two relief steps -- render to fascia to sign tray -- read as relief rather than as flat colour bands. castShadow is set on every component and every cluster; receiveShadow on the deck, the glazing and the facade wall. No ambient occlusion is baked into any base colour.

The fourth entry is the sign itself: the AIS face is an internally lit acrylic lightbox. The plate measures its green at #A0CB1F, brighter than the authored albedo #8FC72C, and that difference is emission rather than paint. It is carried as an emissive term with the canvas as its emissiveMap -- so the white mark glows white and the green field glows green, which is how a lightbox behaves -- and explicitly NOT as scene light, because it must not spill onto the render around it. Intensity was reduced 0.35 -> 0.22 once the map/colour multiply was fixed, since with the colour slot at white the emissive no longer had a darkened base to lift.

NO DEFECT was found at this pass and no value changed. Measurements are re-recorded rather than carried on trust: 1440 triangles / 16000, 12 draw calls / 12, 8 materials / 8, 8 unique geometries / 8; turntable passes with holed=false and covered=true; diagnose_render IoU 0.842, aspect 0.042, scale 0.042, symmetry 0.039, maxDeltaE 14.7; hole-filled silhouette IoU 0.9079. One limitation stated plainly: the harness lights analytically with no environment map and no PMREM, so this pass cannot evaluate how the two metals respond to image-based lighting. That is the same fact that drove the metalness values down at the structural pass, and it is a property of the target -- a browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs is commonly lit analytically for the same performance reason.

PIVOTS: exactly ONE, the root, at base-center on y=0. This is a fixed building shell. Nothing on it articulates: there is no lid that opens, no wheel that turns and no door leaf that swings. The plate does show glazed entrance leaves, and they are deliberately authored as fixed framed glazing rather than as two articulating components, because a named pivot is a PROMISE that a part turns on that axis and the kit would then have to keep it. Declaring door-slide-l and -r here would describe a mechanism this prop does not have. Every non-root component declares animationRole 'structure' and gets no axis. One root pivot on a static prop is the right answer, not a gap.

SOCKETS: exactly ONE, sign-mount, at [0, 3.47, 3.50] on the +Z axis. FINAL BUDGET, measured on the built model by render-model.mjs, not projected: 1440 triangles against 16000, 12 draw calls against 12, 8 materials against 8, 8 unique geometries against 8. Three of the four axes sit exactly at their ceiling and none is over.

The binding axis was never triangles -- the prop uses 9% of its triangle budget -- it was UNIQUE GEOMETRIES, because the generator bakes each component's real dimensions into vertex data via geometry.scale(), so every distinct componentTree box is a genuinely distinct geometry however similar it looks. hero2x allows eight. The structure that made it fit is seven component geometries plus ONE unit BoxGeometry shared by five InstancedMesh clusters carrying 35 boxes between them: framing (14), rooftop plant (8), sign tray return (4), side-wall fittings (5) and parapet coping (4). Authored as components those 35 boxes would have been 35 more geometries and 35 more draw calls on a prop whose ceilings are 8 and 12. That decision had to be made in the blockout: a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

The large triangle headroom is deliberately available for silhouette work and is NOT an invitation to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce. Two things were bought with it during the passes -- the parapet coping cluster and the shopfront framing's transom and meeting stile -- and both went in as cluster instances, costing triangles and draw calls but zero geometries.

comparisonScope.exclusionReason: aluminium is EXCLUDED from the crop comparison, deliberately and on the record, because the comparator cannot produce valid evidence for it from this plate -- not because it failed. A 0.06 m mullion is about 9 px on a 1024 plate, and the comparator's foreground masker consistently keeps the dark flanking GLASS and discards the bright metal: render coverage came back at 0.41 and 0.22 on mullion-centred crops, and the tool itself warns 'foreground mask is tiny; material extraction is likely unreliable' on the plate side. The fairest footprint found -- one mullion with its flanking glass on BOTH sides, coverage 1.0 and 0.74 -- reached deltaE00 11.62 with NO mismatches and overall 0.676, just under the aggregate threshold, and that comparison record is kept in material-compare/aluminium.json. Driving it lower would require darkening the framing to match a crop that is mostly glass, and the plate's framing is itself dark because it is backlit by a dim shop interior this exterior shell does not have -- so matching it would be baking the plate's lighting into base colour, which the material rules forbid. The value WAS still corrected on appearance grounds across three rounds, #B6BABB -> #A5A9AA -> #8E9294, because side by side the rendered mullions read near-white against the plate's mid-grey. The residual gap is reported rather than hidden.
